{"cycle_position": "mid", "runner_up": "late", "what_would_settle_it": "A sequential DRAM average-selling-price decline that management does NOT attribute to mix, arriving together with a sequential fall in consolidated gross margin and a rise in company inventory (in dollars or, better, in disclosed days) — that combination would move me to `late`; conversely, a further sequential gross-margin expansion with DRAM ASPs up sequentially across all four business units would keep me at `mid` with more confidence. Beyond that, the three items the bundle simply does not contain — inventory days for the company and the channel, fab utilisation against its own history, and industry-wide (not Micron) capital expenditure in dollars — are what would convert this from a directional read into a measured one.", "why": "SCOPE NOTE. The bundle is a single document: Micron's Form 10-Q for Q3 FY2025 (quarter ended 2025-05-29, filed 2025-06-26). It contains no <computed_metrics> block, so no ratio, day-count or peer comparison is available to me and I have computed none. Everything below is either quoted from that filing or an inference from quoted material.

=== f) MARGIN POSITION RELATIVE TO THE BUNDLE'S OWN HISTORY (strongest available evidence) ===

F1 FACT [10Q-MDA-CONSOL-TABLE] — "Gross margin | 3,508 | 38% | 2,963 | 37% | 1,832 | 27% | 9,819 | 38% | 2,876 | 17%" (columns: Q3'25, Q2'25, Q3'24, 9M'25, 9M'24).
F2 FACT [10Q-MDA-GM] — "Our consolidated gross margin percentage increased to 38% for the third quarter of 2025 from 37% for the second quarter of 2025, primarily due to an improvement in margins for DRAM products, partially offset by a decrease in margins for NAND products."
F3 FACT [10Q-MDA-GM] — "Our consolidated gross margin for the first nine months of 2024 reflected $987 million of benefit due to lower costs from the sale of inventories written down to their net realizable value in 2023."
F4 FACT [10Q-RF-GM] — "in 2023, we recorded aggregate charges of $1.83 billion to write down the carrying value of our inventories to their estimated net realizable value."
F5 FACT [10Q-MDA-INDUSTRY] — "In 2024 and for the first nine months of 2025, we experienced substantial improvements in revenue, pricing, and margins as compared to 2023, reflecting demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI, which resulted in a substantially improved industry supply and demand balance."

I6 INFERENCE (from F1, F3, F4, F5) — 38% is the highest gross margin in the four periods the bundle discloses, and the bundle's implied starting point is a loss-making 2023 in which inventory was written below cost. The margin series is therefore an unbroken recovery, and it is still rising at the margin (37% → 38%), not flattening or rolling over.
GAP — the bundle gives no gross margin for any period before 9M FY2024 other than the qualitative 2023 write-down. I cannot place 38% against a full-cycle range; I can only say it is the highest of the four disclosed quarters/periods.

=== a) REALISED PRICES / ASPs AGAINST THEIR RANGE ===

F7 FACT [10Q-MDA-REV] — "Sales of DRAM products increased 51% primarily due to a mid-20% range increase in average selling prices and an increase in bit shipments in the low-20% range." (Q3'25 vs Q3'24)
F8 FACT [10Q-MDA-REV] — "Sales of DRAM products increased 15% primarily due to an over 20% increase in bit shipments, partially offset by a low-single-digit percent range decrease in average selling prices primarily due to a higher consumer-oriented revenue mix." (Q3'25 vs Q2'25)
F9 FACT [10Q-MDA-REV] — "Sales of NAND products increased 4% primarily due to a low-30% range increase in bit shipments, partially offset by a low-20% range decrease in average selling prices." (Q3'25 vs Q3'24)
F10 FACT [10Q-MDA-REV] — "Sales of NAND products increased 16% primarily due to a mid-20% range increase in bit shipments, partially offset by a high-single-digit percent range decrease in average selling prices." (Q3'25 vs Q2'25)
F11 FACT [10Q-RF-ASP] — "In the past five years, annual percentage changes in DRAM average selling prices have ranged from plus low-teen percentage range to a minus high-40% range. In the past five years, annual percentage changes in NAND average selling prices have ranged from plus low-30% to a minus low-50% range."

I12 INFERENCE (from F7, F11) — the 9M DRAM ASP move the filing reports ("a high-40% range increase in average selling prices", 9M'25 vs 9M'24) and the Q3 mid-20% YoY increase both sit above the top of the five-year annual range the company itself publishes (plus low-teen). The DRAM price move in this upcycle is therefore larger than anything in the company's own stated five-year band.
I13 INFERENCE (from F8, F10) — the sequential direction has already turned negative for both products: DRAM ASP down low-single-digit and NAND ASP down high-single-digit quarter-on-quarter. For DRAM the company attributes this to mix, not to underlying price; for NAND it offers no mix explanation.
GAP — F11 gives the range of *annual percentage changes*, not the range of ASP *levels*. The bundle contains no ASP level in any period. Item (a) as literally asked — realised price against its level range — cannot be answered; the best available substitute is the rate-of-change comparison in I12.

=== b) INVENTORY, COMPANY AND CHANNEL ===

F14 FACT [10Q-NOTE-INV] — Inventories: "Finished goods | $1,223 | $1,308 / Work in process | $6,695 | $6,774 / Raw materials and supplies | $809 | $793 / $8,727 | $8,875" (May 29 2025 vs Aug 29 2024).
F15 FACT [10Q-CF] — "Inventories | 148 | (125)" (nine-month cash-flow change, FY25 vs FY24) — i.e. inventory was a source of cash in 9M FY2025.
F16 FACT [10Q-MDA-INDUSTRY] — "In the third quarter of 2025, NAND revenue improved from the prior quarter due to improvements across end markets, in particular strong bit growth in consumer-oriented markets due to reduced customer inventories. We saw reduced demand from NAND customers in the first two quarters of 2025 as customers reduced inventory to align with their end customers."
F17 FACT [10Q-MDA-BU] — "MBU revenue increased 45% primarily due to increases in bit shipments driven by reduced customer inventories and strong demand from DRAM content growth, partially offset by declines in average selling prices for both mobile DRAM and NAND."

I18 INFERENCE (from F14, F15) — company inventory fell in absolute dollars over nine months while quarterly revenue rose from $6,811m (Q3'24) to $9,301m (Q3'25). Inventory is not building against a rising revenue base.
I19 INFERENCE (from F16, F17) — the channel description is of customers *finishing* a destock in mobile and consumer-oriented end markets during FY2025, and that destock ending is the stated driver of Q3 bit shipment growth. Channel inventory being drawn down to a point where restocking begins is an early-to-mid-cycle marker for those end markets, not a late one.
GAP — no days-of-inventory figure is disclosed for Micron and none for the channel. The bundle contains no <computed_metrics> block from which to take one, and I have not computed one. Item (b) is answered directionally in dollars only.

=== c) CAPACITY UTILISATION AGAINST ITS OWN HISTORY ===

F20 FACT [10Q-MDA-INDUSTRY] — "We continue to prudently manage our NAND supply, including the levels of our capital investment, the pace of ramp of our new technology node, and fab utilization consistent with our demand growth."
F21 FACT [10Q-RF-GM] — "higher manufacturing costs per gigabit due to fabrication facility underutilization, lower wafer output, and insufficient volume to run new technology nodes to achieve cost optimization" is listed as a factor that may limit cost reduction.

I22 INFERENCE (from F20) — Micron describes itself as still restraining NAND fab utilisation deliberately as of Q3 FY2025. A producer withholding utilisation is not operating at a supply-constrained peak in that product line.
GAP — no utilisation percentage, no wafer starts, no capacity figure is given for any period. Item (c) has no quantitative answer in this bundle. This is a material gap: utilisation against history is one of the cleaner cycle discriminators and it is simply absent.

=== d) ORDER PATTERNS: LEAD TIMES, BACKLOG, CANCELLATIONS, CONTRACT DURATION ===

F23 FACT [10Q-NOTE-REV] — "Substantially all contracts with our customers are short-term in duration at fixed, negotiated prices with payment generally due shortly after delivery."
F24 FACT [10Q-NOTE-REV] — "As of May 29, 2025, our future performance obligations beyond one year were $143 million, which included customer prepayments and other contract liabilities."
F25 FACT [10Q-NOTE-REV] — "As of May 29, 2025 and August 29, 2024, customer prepayments made to secure product supply in future periods and other contract liabilities were $146 million and $907 million, respectively... Revenue recognized during the first nine months of 2025 from the beginning balance as of August 29, 2024 included $777 million from shipments against customer prepayments and other contract liabilities."
F26 FACT [10Q-RF-SUPPLY] — "some of our components have long lead-times, requiring us to place orders up to a year in advance of anticipated demand."

I27 INFERENCE (from F23, F24) — Micron does not disclose a backlog and its contracts are structurally short-dated, so backlog and lead time are not observable in this filing. F26 concerns Micron's own inbound component lead times, not its customers' lead times for Micron product.
I28 INFERENCE (from F25) — the prepayment balance fell from $907m to $146m, with $777m of it consumed by shipments during the nine months. The balance was drawn down rather than replenished at a comparable rate. Two readings are consistent with this and the bundle does not separate them: customers no longer feel obliged to prepay to secure supply (a softening signal), or the prepayments simply ran their contractual course. I cannot distinguish them.
GAP — no cancellation disclosure, no lead-time disclosure, no backlog. Item (d) is largely unanswerable from this bundle.

=== e) INDUSTRY-WIDE CAPITAL EXPENDITURE — THE LEADING VARIABLE ===

F29 FACT [10Q-CF] — "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment | (10,199) | (5,266)" (9M FY2025 vs 9M FY2024).
F30 FACT [10Q-MDA-LIQ] — "We estimate capital expenditures in 2025 for property, plant, and equipment, net of proceeds from government incentives, to be approximately $14 billion."
F31 FACT [10Q-BS-NOTE-PPE] — "Construction in progress(2) | 4,937 | 3,444" and "Accounts payable and accrued expenses ... Property, plant, and equipment | 4,370 | 2,925".
F32 FACT [10Q-RF-COMPETITION] — "We and our competitors generally seek to increase supply to address growing market demands, improve yields, and reduce die size, which could result in significant increases in worldwide supply and downward pressure on prices... Our competitors may increase capital expenditures resulting in future increases in worldwide supply. We, and some of our competitors, have plans to ramp, or are constructing or ramping, production at new fabrication facilities."
F33 FACT [10Q-RF-COMPETITION] — "we face the threat of increasing competition and oversupply due to significant investment in the semiconductor industry by the Chinese government and various state-owned or affiliated entities, such as YMTC and CXMT."
F34 FACT [10Q-MDA-LIQ] — "Construction of the fab began in October 2023, with first DRAM wafer output projected in the second half of calendar 2027."
F35 FACT [10Q-MDA-LIQ] — "In January 2025, we broke ground on an HBM advanced packaging facility in Singapore to meaningfully expand our total advanced packaging capacity beginning in calendar 2027."
F36 FACT [10Q-MDA-LIQ] — "Our announced plan for New York includes construction of a leading-edge DRAM memory manufacturing site, consisting of up to four fabs to be built over the next 20-plus years... with production anticipated to ramp after the completion of the second Idaho fab."

I37 INFERENCE (from F29, F30, F31) — Micron's own capital spending roughly doubled year on year on a nine-month basis, with construction in progress and PP&E payables both up sharply. The company is building, not starving.
I38 INFERENCE (from F32, F33) — the filing asserts, qualitatively, that competitors are also constructing or ramping and that state-backed Chinese capacity is expanding. The industry is in a building phase.
I39 INFERENCE (from F34, F35, F36) — the DRAM wafer capacity and advanced packaging capacity now being funded is stated to begin output in calendar 2027 or later. The supply that this capex creates is not yet in the market as of the quarter under review.
GAP — the bundle contains no dollar figure, wafer figure or growth rate for any competitor's capital expenditure, and no industry aggregate. Item (e) is answered by direction from the company's own spend plus the company's own qualitative characterisation of peers; it is not a measured industry number, and I have treated the peer element as unchecked.

=== THE DISCRIMINATING OBSERVATION: THE PORTFOLIO IS SPLIT ===

F40 FACT [10Q-MDA-BU-OPINC] — "CNBU | $2,182 | 43% | $1,919 | 42% | $442 | 17% | $5,812 | 41% | $73 | 1%" (operating income and margin: Q3'25, Q2'25, Q3'24, 9M'25, 9M'24).
F41 FACT [10Q-MDA-BU-OPINC] — "SBU | (9) | (1)% | 24 | 2% | 76 | 6% | 362 | 8% | (631) | (22)%".
F42 FACT [10Q-MDA-BU] — "SBU operating income (loss) deteriorated for the third quarter of 2025 as compared to the third quarter of 2024 primarily due to decreases in selling prices for NAND."
F43 FACT [10Q-MDA-BU] — "MBU revenue decreased 2% for the third quarter of 2025 as compared to the third quarter of 2024 primarily due to declines in DRAM and NAND average selling prices" and "EBU revenue decreased 5% and 4%, respectively, primarily due to declines in average selling prices".
F44 FACT [10Q-NOTE-CONC] — Revenue by market segment, 9M: "Data center and networking | 55% | 30% / Mobile | 15% | 25% / PC, graphics, and other | 15% | 25% / Intelligent edge – automotive, industrial, and consumer embedded | 15% | 20%".
F45 FACT [10Q-MDA-BU] — "CNBU revenue increased 11% primarily due to higher sales of HBM products, which increased nearly 50%, along with growth in our high-capacity DRAM and low-power server DRAM."
F46 FACT [10Q-RF-PRODUCTS] — "If we or our competitors increase HBM supply at a rate that outpaces HBM demand, conversion of HBM capacity to supply other DRAM products could result in significant supply-demand imbalances. Due to the higher performance and more complex manufacturing process, HBM requires a higher number of wafers to produce the same number of bits as conventional DRAM in the same technology node. This could lead to declines in average selling prices for our DRAM products."

I47 INFERENCE (from F40–F45) — the aggregate 38% gross margin is not a broad-based condition. One unit (CNBU, data-centre/HBM) is at a 43% operating margin and rising; the NAND storage unit is at a 1% operating *loss* and deteriorating sequentially and year on year on falling prices; mobile and embedded revenue are both *below* their prior-year quarter on falling ASPs. Data-centre exposure went from 30% to 55% of revenue while every other end market shrank as a share.
I48 INFERENCE (from I47) — a late-cycle or peak reading normally requires strength across the portfolio with supply catching up everywhere. Here three of four end markets have prices that have already fallen and two of them have revenue below the prior year, while the fourth is at a record margin. That pattern is characteristic of a cycle in which one segment leads and the rest are only now emerging from destocking (F16, F17) — i.e. mid-cycle with dispersion — rather than a synchronised top.

=== THE TRAP, STATED EXPLICITLY ===

I49 INFERENCE (from F1, I6) — trailing earnings are at their highest in the bundle's disclosed history and still expanding sequentially. That means any trailing-multiple view of this business is at its most flattering right now, and mechanically I am on the *dangerous* side of the trap, not the safe one: if this is in fact the peak, trailing figures will look best exactly at the point of maximum risk.
I50 INFERENCE (from I39, I19, I47) — what stops me short of calling it the peak is that the three things that normally turn a peak into a downcycle are, on this evidence, not yet present: the funded capacity does not produce until calendar 2027 or later (I39), customer inventories are being drawn down rather than rebuilt (I19), and the majority of end markets have not yet participated in the price recovery (I47).
I51 INFERENCE (from F41, F42, F43, I13) — the counter-case is real and I am not dismissing it: NAND prices are already falling on both comparisons, NAND's business unit is at an operating loss, and mobile and embedded ASPs are down year on year. If DRAM follows NAND, the correct label becomes `late` and then `peak`, and the margin series (F1) will be the last thing to turn.

ASSUMPTION 1 — I am treating "mid" as meaning: recovery from the 2023 trough is established and margins are still expanding, capacity to end the cycle has been ordered but has not yet produced, and end-market participation is still broadening. The bundle does not define these terms; a reader using a definition anchored on absolute margin level rather than on supply timing and end-market breadth would reasonably read the same facts as `late`.
ASSUMPTION 2 — I am treating Micron's own characterisation of competitor behaviour (F32, F33) as evidence about the industry. It is a risk-factor statement by an interested party, not an independent industry capex series, and the reader is entitled to discount it.

NET — `mid`, held with the explicit acknowledgement that items (b) inventory days, (c) utilisation, and (d) backlog/lead times are absent from the bundle, and that item (a) is available only as rates of change, not levels."}
